transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been bothering you or what brings you here today?

Well, thank you for seeing me, Doctor. I really appreciate you taking the time. I, um... I hope I'm not making a bigger deal out of this than I should be. I always try to be a team player, you know? 

But it’s just... well, it’s a situation at work. For over a year now, I’ve been trying to get someone to just... take it seriously. They started this new ticket rotation system, along with these new security audits, and... I know how this might sound, and I really don't want to come across as difficult or anything, but it's pretty clear they're being used to build a paper trail against me. 

I’ve tried to explain it to management, very reasonably, but they just keep pulling up the system logs and telling me it’s just standard company policy. It's been very stressful trying to navigate it without causing a fuss. I hope I'm explaining that in a way that makes sense?
Can you tell me more about why you believe the ticket rotation system and security audits are being used against you?

Well, I... I know how it sounds. I really do. I don't want to come across like one of those disgruntled employees who complains about every little workflow change, you know? I've always prided myself on being adaptable. 

But... well, the way these specific tickets are routed to me, and how they always seem to trigger those security audits... it just feels very deliberate. Like I mentioned, I’ve been trying for over a year to get someone to just look at it and take it seriously. I’ll sit down with management, very respectfully, and they just... they pull up the system logs on the screen. They point to the data and tell me it’s just standard company policy, that it's all automated. 

But when you've been in IT support as long as I have, you can tell when a system is being, well, manipulated to build a paper trail against you. I just... I don't want to make a fuss or cause any trouble for my supervisors, but it's very hard to ignore when you feel like you're being set up. Does that make sense? I really hope I'm not sounding too unreasonable...
Can you tell me if you believe this paper trail is being created to harm you in a specific way, and if you think others are involved in this plan against you?

Oh, goodness, "harm" is a very strong word. I... I wouldn't want to accuse anyone of trying to actually harm me. That sounds a bit too dramatic, doesn't it? I really try to see the best in my colleagues. 

I honestly don't know what the specific end goal is with all of it. Maybe they just want to push me into early retirement? I'm 60 now, so maybe they just want someone younger in the support role... but I really don't know for sure. I haven't quite figured that part out, to be completely honest with you. 

And as for other people being involved... I definitely don't think there's some big group sitting around a conference table plotting against me or anything like that. I don't really know exactly who would be orchestrating it. I just see the results in the ticket queues and the audit flags. 

I hope that's an okay answer? I'm sorry I don't have a more specific explanation for you... I know you're trying to understand, and I hope I'm giving you the right kind of information?
Have you experienced anything else unusual lately, like hearing voices, seeing things others don't, feeling unusually down or hopeless, or having bursts of high energy or irritability?

Oh, my. No, definitely nothing like that. I... I really hope I haven't given you the impression that I'm, well, losing touch with reality or anything. I certainly don't hear voices or see things that aren't there. My mind is perfectly clear, I promise. 

And as for my mood... well, naturally I'm a little stressed about the ticket situation at work, just because I want to do a good job and it's hard when you feel scrutinized, but I wouldn't say I feel hopeless at all. And I'm definitely not having bursts of energy or getting irritable with anyone. I always try to keep an even keel and be pleasant with my coworkers, no matter what. 

I hope that's reassuring to hear? I really am just a normal guy trying to navigate this one specific work issue... I hope I'm answering these questions correctly for you?
Outside of your concerns at work, do you ever feel like there are things you know to be true that others don’t seem to understand or believe, even when they have no reason not to?

Oh, no... no, definitely not. My life outside of the office is very, well, it's very ordinary, really. I just go home, maybe watch a little television, tend to my garden... I certainly don't have any strange ideas or secrets that other people don't get. 

My friends and family, we all see eye to eye on things. There's no tension or misunderstandings there at all. It really is just that one specific issue with the ticketing system at the office. Everything else in my life is completely fine, I promise. 

I hope that's a good thing? I just want to make sure I'm not making my situation seem worse or more complicated than it actually is. I'm really just a regular guy dealing with a frustrating office environment. Did that answer your question okay?
Have you ever had any beliefs or ideas that you are absolutely certain are true, even when others—like your friends or family—don’t seem to share them or understand them?

Oh, um, I feel like maybe we just talked about that a little bit? I... I really don't have anything like that going on. I'm sorry if I'm repeating myself, I just want to be sure I'm giving you what you need. 

But no, my family and I, we're very much on the same page about everything. I don't have any, you know, strange convictions or... or grand ideas that they don't understand. I'm a very grounded person, really. I just like my routine, my garden, my quiet evenings. 

I hope it's okay that I don't have a more interesting answer for you? I just want to be completely honest, and the truth is, outside of that one frustrating thing at work, my life is very simple and straightforward. I'm doing okay answering these, right? I just want to be helpful.

Do you ever feel certain about something at work—like the ticket system being used against you—even when there’s no clear evidence to support it, and you can’t shake the feeling no matter how much you think about it?

Well, um... I wouldn't say there's no evidence, exactly, but... I know it might sound a little strange to other people. I really hope I don't come across as difficult or, well, paranoid, because I'm honestly not. I try very hard to be a good employee. 

But, yes, that is actually sort of why I'm here. For over a year now, I've just been trying to get someone to take it seriously... it's the new ticket rotation, and these security audits they've been running. I just know they're being used to build a paper trail against me. Management keeps sitting me down and showing me the system logs, and they promise me it’s just standard policy. And I always nod and agree with them in the room, because I want to be cooperative, you know? I'd hate to cause a fuss or seem insubordinate. 

But even after they show me all that, I just can't shake the feeling that it's directed at me. I really hope that doesn't make me sound unreasonable to you? I'm just trying to protect my livelihood and do my job well... I hope it's okay that I'm sharing this with you?

Even though management has shown you system logs indicating the ticket rotation and audits are automated and standard policy, do you still feel certain—deep down—that it's really being used to target you?

Well, yes... yes, I do. I mean, I know we just touched on this, and I really, really hope I'm not coming across as stubborn or—or unwilling to listen to reason. I don't want to be a problem employee, I really don't. 

But... yes, deep down, I am certain. For over a year, I've just been so stressed, trying to get someone, anyone, to take this seriously. Management shows me the logs, they point to the timestamps, and they tell me it's all automated policy... and like I said, I nod and I smile because I want them to think I'm a team player. But the minute I walk out of that office, I just know. The way the tickets are routed, the timing of the security audits... it's all just too specific. It's a paper trail, and it's meant for me. 

I know it probably sounds silly to you, a man my age getting so worked up over computer logs. I hope you don't think less of me for it? I just... I can't turn off that feeling that I'm being targeted, no matter what they show me. Does that make sense? I'm trying my best to explain it clearly for you.
Can you tell me if you’ve ever had a thought like this before—where you felt targeted or singled out at work—when there wasn’t clear proof, and how did you handle it in the past?

Oh, um... no, I really haven't. I've been working in IT for a long time, and I've always had a very good relationship with my managers and coworkers. I'm usually the one people come to when they need help fixing things, you know? I pride myself on being reliable and easy to work with. 

I don't think I've ever felt this way before. That's why this whole situation with the ticket system has been so upsetting for me. I'm usually very level-headed about work. I just do my job, help the users, and go home to my garden. 

I hope it doesn't seem like I'm someone who complains a lot or has a history of causing trouble at work? Because I really don't. This is the first time I've ever felt like I was being pushed out or singled out like this. I've always had glowing performance reviews before this last year. I'm answering your questions okay, aren't I? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right context.
Have you ever felt in the past, outside of this current situation at work, that others were deliberately trying to undermine or sabotage you?

Oh, goodness, no. No, never. Outside of this... well, this whole mess at the office, I get along with pretty much everyone. I have my neighbors, and a few friends from my gardening group, and we all get along wonderfully. 

I really don't want you to think I'm the sort of person who goes around looking for enemies, because I'm honestly not. I've always tried to be very accommodating and friendly to everyone I meet. I hope you believe me when I say that? It's really just this one specific thing at work that's been so troubling. I've never felt like anyone was trying to sabotage me before this. 

Does that help clear things up? I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need for your notes.
